questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Academic and career opportunities was of course a big factor, but the initial motivation to go was the need to try something new and get out of the comfort zone, and only after did I realize that an exchange can be really good for academic and career. So what motivated to go on an exchange was really just to challenge myself and try something different (not necessarily to explore new cultures).

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The spoken language, as I really wanted to improve my French.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy and surprisingly was most of the information in English.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome week where we got a lot of information, and then every continent had a supervisor connected so if we had any questions, it was super easy to E-mail him and get answers to questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy since I started to look for housing early.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is nothing since most of the university's housing options are close to the faculties, and when you get a option to get housing you can choose where you want to live so just pick somewhere close to your faculty or at least close to downtown.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
So this part was kinda of confusing for me but you have the courses you have found prior to your arrival in Geneve and then you attend these courses for something like 3 weeks where you then can change or confirm these courses. You can have courses form max 2 different faculties.

Since I had chosen 2 or 3 courses that were either not offered anyway or cancelled I had to change my learning agreement, which stressed me as I then had to find 2-3 new courses and make it add up to 30 ECTS. But it fortunately all worked out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The mobility supervisor is always there to help, either by a meeting or by mail, he helped me a lot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Actually not too succesfull which also resulting in taking courses I wasn't really super interested in, but I think this is because of my background in pharmacy, which the university didn't really (a few) provided English tought courses in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't talk for all educations but if you have a pharmaceutical background you should maybe don't go to Geneve unless you speak French or that you're super strong and have a liking for chemistry since I reckon this was the only subject that the university provided multiple English tought courses in. And from experience from my friends, I can tell that if your education is economics, global health or law the amount of courses won't be a problem at all.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was actually very high, higher than what I expected since I checked the university's ranking prior to my arrival and got the idea that the level maybe was lower than what I was used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style with predominantly lectures aligned well with what I already was used to. Though the lectures/courses tended to have fewer students so the classes was always in class rooms and not auditories, but I guess that correlates with my courses being not the most popular ones.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Physical chemistry of polymers and bio-macromolecules
Current Topics in Chemical Biology and Biochemistry
Drug Policy and Global Health
Quantitative methods in Global Health - epidemiology
And then two French classes.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked Current Topics in Chemical Biology and Biochemistry since you get a introduction by top scientist from both UNIGE and EPFL to a lot of emerging strategies and innovations in the biochemistry/pharmaceutical industry which was really interesting this course really taught me a lot of new things. furthermore was this course without exams, since there was presentations once a week, which was nice as you only had to present 3-4 times throughout the course. 

I recommend the Drug Policy and Global Health course as this course gives a really nice political and diplomatic insight in drug regulation, which is really relevant if you want to pursue a career in RA.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were some fees related to the process of getting my permit but im not sure of how much it mounted up to.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Everything is expensive but I mean compared to Denmark its was not way more expensive (since Denmark is expensive too). 
Since they don't have the 25 % moms, clothes and stuff like that was a bit cheaper, but overall very similar to Denmark tbh.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were A LOT of non academic opportunities, fitness/gym (cheap), futsal every monday and thursday and honestly A LOT of other opportunities. I wanted to join more things than what I did, but didn't had the time. But yeah I was really really satisfied with the non-academic opportunities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
So so many I can't even type all that if you want to view all of their activities you can go to "
https://vie-de-campus.unige.ch/catalogue?tags=SPORT
" where they have an A-Z list with all they offer (which is literally everything you could think of).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Since it's a French speaking region I would recommend the futsal activity since it really doesn't require you to be able to speak French in order to participate. There were a lot of other things too I think would be nice but my top recommendation is futsal. And the level was really like average so everybody could join even girls. Me and the other Danish guys went there ones and teamed up agains the rest, really funny.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: A lot of options to hike. You shouldn't forget your ski gear since there are a lot of nearby ski places and the school even arrange ski tours. Go to France (walking distance ;)) maybe Annecy (very beautiful). Go to the other big cities very easy with train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy basically the same culture as in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Yeah go to the ESN (Erasmus) events very easy to find friends there. I didn't really go to many of the events though. I found the most of my friends through football.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Idk maybe that it was very international, so English was totally fine for most I talked to.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing through the university since this will make the whole so much easier economically in a city were most things are really expensive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I can't really say one thing but I feel like it has been really rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The problems with finding what courses to attend.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
